changes: A mistyped API address now returns a proper 'no such endpoint' instead of quietly handing back the web page with a 200
Vault detection no longer looks in a folder named after the author's own project directory
Eight internal helpers stopped being published as part of the library's public interface
The plan now marks what was designed but never built - collections, per-snip notes, quote cards, the Obsidian deep link and the evaluation harness
The security notes were re-audited and a claim that had gone stale was corrected
whatToTest: Nothing user-facing should have changed; this release is repository housekeeping before the code goes public

changes: The meaning index now keeps itself current: snips added by a sync are embedded on their own, instead of waiting to be noticed
It also catches up shortly after the app starts, for snips that arrived while it was closed
Nothing was ever losing your vectors - they simply stopped being added after the last time the button was pressed
A first build is still a deliberate press, because it downloads a model and takes about 45 minutes for 30,000 snips
Rebuild now asks before re-embedding a finished index
whatToTest: Sync now with new snips in your vault - the dashboard should show it embedding them without being asked
Dashboard - Meaning index - it should say 'ready' and leave you alone

changes: First run is cleaner: no dead navigation links before you've chosen a vault, and no changelog for a version you've never used
A mistyped vault path now tells you which mistake you made - the folder isn't there, or it holds no Snipd export
Errors from the app now reach you in its own words rather than as a status code
The NotebookLM export refuses to write a folder with nothing in it
New on the Ask page: package your whole library for NotebookLM as Markdown files it will actually accept
Group by show, by category, or by date - the file names become the citations NotebookLM shows you
Files are kept under NotebookLM's 500,000-word limit, and the file count under its sources-per-notebook cap, with a live count before you commit
Writes a guide explaining that the quotes are transcribed speech, which hosted models otherwise mistake for your own writing
Writes step-by-step import instructions, deliberately outside the folder you upload
whatToTest: Ask - 'Package this library for NotebookLM' - try 'One file per category', which fits even the free plan
Create the import folder; it should open in Explorer with a sources folder and HOW-TO-IMPORT.md beside it

changes: Fixed the app freezing and every page going blank: clicking inside the console window it starts in puts Windows into 'Select' mode, which stops the server dead the next time it prints anything
The server now writes to a log file instead of that window, so a stray click can no longer reach it
When the server does stop answering, the app says so in plain words instead of showing empty pages
Requests give up after 20 seconds rather than hanging forever; slow ones (Ask, backups, restore, sync) still get five minutes
whatToTest: Start Resurface.bat, then click and drag inside the black window - the app should keep working
Close the window while the app is open in the browser; you should get a red bar saying it isn't responding, which clears itself if you start it again

changes: Backups are now checked against the database they were copied from - a snapshot that quietly lost data can no longer pass as good
Each snapshot records what it contained, so a restore can tell whether the file still holds it
The write-ahead log is capped at 64 MB instead of growing without limit
Asking for absurd page sizes no longer dumps the whole library in one response
Reviewing or re-labelling a snip that doesn't exist now says so instead of failing with a server error
An out-of-range month in Wrapped is rejected rather than silently answered with the whole year
whatToTest: Dashboard - Backups - Back up now; the panel should report the snips and vectors it verified
Everything should behave exactly as before; this release is mostly about what happens when things go wrong

changes: Filter any search by who made the snip — you, or Snipd's template — in all three search modes
'Made by me' works on its own with no search text, so you can just browse the 4,239 snips you wrote
New dashboard panel shows the split, and lets you settle the borderline ones yourself; your answer is permanent
Starred loads 4x faster: it was downloading every full note to render a five-line preview
Fixed timestamps showing as NaN:NaN in the borderline list
whatToTest: Dashboard → 'Who made your snips' → 'Browse the ones you made'
Search anything, then set the dropdown to 'Made by me' — try it in Smart and Keyword
Dashboard → settle a couple of borderline snips; the count should drop and they shouldn't come back
Starred should feel noticeably quicker to load

changes: Resurface now checks its own database regularly and tells you the moment anything is wrong, naming the backup to restore
Keyboard use fixed: there was no visible focus indicator at all, and no way to skip past the navigation
The Dashboard and Search pages had no heading for screen readers to announce; they do now
Motion is reduced automatically if your system asks for it
New INSTALL.md: first run, updating, starting at login, every setting, and what to do when something breaks
whatToTest: Tab through the app with the keyboard — you should see where you are, and 'Skip to content' should appear first
Dashboard → Backups should say 'checked and sound'
Read INSTALL.md and try the autostart steps if you want it running at login

changes: Automatic backups: a full snapshot once a day, and a small record of your review history, bookmarks and category names saved constantly
Every snapshot is opened and integrity-checked before it's kept — a backup nobody has verified is only a guess
Restore any snapshot from the dashboard in a couple of seconds, without stopping the app
Restoring never deletes what it replaces: the old database is moved aside, not removed
The write-ahead log is now folded back in periodically, so it can't grow into the hundreds of megabytes where checkpointing started failing
Start Resurface.bat now repairs a half-installed embedding library instead of starting into a broken state
whatToTest: Dashboard → Backups: it should already list a snapshot taken shortly after startup
Press 'Back up now' — it should finish in a few seconds and report the snips it verified
Press Restore on a snapshot, confirm, and check search and Review still work afterwards
Look in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Resurface\backups — the work-*.json files are small enough to keep forever

changes: Starred snips now show a five-line preview and expand in place to the full note and transcript, like everywhere else
Ask: each cited source expands to the whole snip on the page, so following a citation no longer means leaving Ask
Fixed the update script leaving the local embedding library half-installed, which made the meaning index look empty and rebuild itself
whatToTest: Starred → a favorite snip should show a few lines, then 'Read the full snip' should open the rest in place
Ask something, then expand a source to read the full snip without leaving the page
After the next update, the meaning index should still show its full count — no surprise rebuild

changes: Read any snip where you find it: every snip in search, review, the digest and tag pages now expands in place instead of sending you to its episode
Expansions are collapsed by default and load only when you open one, so long lists stay fast
Where the notes are already on screen, expanding goes straight to the transcript rather than asking for a second click
whatToTest: Search something, then expand a result — the full transcript should appear without leaving the page
Review → expand a card; a hand-made snip should show its whole note inline
Collapse it again — the page should return exactly to where it was

changes: Daily review: a handful of snips a day out of 32,000, chosen so the ones you'd forgotten come back
Keeping a snip widens when it returns — 3 days, then a week, three weeks, two months, six months
'Stop showing' takes a snip out of review only; it stays in your library, search, stats and exports
Every card says why it was picked, and 3 of the 5 are snips you made by hand
This week: a digest of what you snipped, which themes rose against last week, and older snips never resurfaced
Subscribe to the digest as a feed — no account, no email, nothing sent anywhere
On this day: what you were listening to on this date in earlier months
Surprise me: one click for the oldest thing you've never had resurfaced
Wrapped can now be saved as an image
The app and the command line no longer open the database at the same time — a sync is handed to the running app instead
whatToTest: Review → read the five cards and their reasons; press Keep on one and reload — it should be gone for 3 days
Review → 'Stop showing' on something, then search for it: it should still be there
This week → check the rising themes against what you actually listened to
This week → 'Surprise me' a few times; it should reach back into January
This week → 'subscribe by feed' and add it to any RSS reader
Wrapped → 'Save as image'
Run 'npm run import' while the app is open — it should hand the sync over rather than open the database

changes: Auto vs. manual snips: Resurface now tells the snips Snipd made from the ones you made — by the shape of the note, never its length of audio
Only 189 of 32,212 snips are borderline, and they're listed for you to settle; whatever you decide sticks, even after a re-import
Topics are named after ideas, not speakers: a label that used to end in a host's name now ends in the subject instead
Topic labels drop names your export states outright, and any word confined to fewer shows than the topic it labels
Ask: connecting a local model now checks it actually works first, so it can never sit in a connected-but-broken state
Ask: the local-model panel is always visible, says in plain words what's wrong and how to fix it, and can disconnect
Wrapped: 'Your week' says what it's counting, and switches between snips, episodes and time listened
Fixed a database corruption bug: workers no longer run schema changes alongside the main app, and writers wait their turn
whatToTest: Open the most recent episode — your two hand-made snips should read as manual, the rest as auto
Topics → Find topics, then read the labels: no host or guest names should appear
Ask → the local model panel at the bottom: press Test connection and read what it tells you
Wrapped → 'Your week' → switch to Time listened, then Episodes
Search and Starred should be unchanged — auto/manual deliberately does not affect ranking

changes: Ask: put a question to your own library and get an answer with a citation on every line — passages are quoted verbatim, so nothing can be invented
Optional local model: connect Ollama for a written summary over the same cited passages; without it Ask still works
Categories: your own editable taxonomy, seeded from discovered topics — rename, merge, delete, and pin or remove individual snips
Pinned snips define what a category means, and re-assigning never undoes your corrections
Wrapped: every leaderboard now shows the top 5 with a dropdown for 10, 25 or all
Wrapped: new leaderboards for most favorites, busiest days, biggest months, longest, most-snipped and densest episodes
Wrapped: view any single month, not just the whole year — compared against the same month last year
whatToTest: Ask → put a real question to your library and check the sources actually answer it
Wrapped → pick a month from the new dropdown; the headline and every list should follow
Wrapped → open any leaderboard's Top 5 dropdown and switch to 25
Categories → Seed from topics, then Re-assign all snips (about a minute)
Open a category, remove a snip that doesn't belong, then re-assign — it should stay removed
Rename a category to something meaningful to you, and merge two that overlap

changes: Topics: Resurface groups your snips by meaning and names each group after the words that set it apart — 36 topics across 32k snips, found in about 15 seconds
Map: every snip as a point, colored by topic; pick a topic to light up its island and read its most typical snips
Topic pages list the most central snips first — the clearest examples of what each topic actually is
Smart search modes now report what their counts mean, so Keyword, Smart and Meaning are comparable at a glance
Smart search works on a partially built index instead of silently falling back to keyword
whatToTest: Topics → Find topics (needs the meaning index; takes about a minute)
Open a topic and read its most typical snips — do the labels match what's inside?
Map → pick a topic from the dropdown; its island lights up and the rest fades
Hover points on the map to see which snip is where
Search 'how do you pray' in Keyword, then Smart, then Meaning only — the results and the counts should now differ visibly
Rebuild topics after a big sync to fold new snips in

changes: Meaning index: Resurface can now find snips by idea, not just by wording — built locally on your CPU, nothing uploaded
Similar snips on every snip: neighbors from anywhere in your library, excluding the same episode
Smart search blends keywords with meaning (reciprocal rank fusion); 'Meaning only' and 'Keyword' modes are one dropdown away
Build/Resume/Stop the index from the dashboard with live progress — it runs in the background and never blocks the app
Index builds are throttled: Gentle (default) uses about one core at below-normal priority, so your PC stays usable — and it's barely slower than Fast
The index is resumable: stopping keeps every vector already built, and new snips are embedded incrementally
Fixed: a UTF-8 byte-order mark in package.json broke 'Update Resurface.bat' builds
whatToTest: Dashboard → Meaning index → Build index (first run downloads a ~25 MB model, then ~55 minutes for 32k snips in Gentle)
While it builds, keep using your PC — Task Manager should show roughly one core busy; Stop and Resume should lose nothing
Open any episode and click 'Similar snips' under a snip you know well
Search something you'd struggle to word exactly, e.g. 'how do I stop worrying about the future'
Compare the Smart and Keyword modes on the same query — Smart should surface snips that never use your words
Try 'Meaning only' for a vague theme like 'assurance in suffering'

changes: Snipd tags are first-class: a Tags page, clickable #chips everywhere, tag filters with live counts in search, and tag:chat syntax
Search now works with tags alone — no keywords needed — and every result names its podcast first
Starred rows lead with the show and episode instead of burying them under the snip title
'Confirmed listening' is now 'Snip time' (audio your snips captured); listening time is the headline number, with its overcount caveat in a tooltip
Short-form shows finally show up: rank Wrapped by hours/episodes/snips/density, plus a snips-per-hour leaderboard and a short-vs-long-form split

Wrapped shows up to all 163 shows and adds ~15 new stats: busiest day, longest streak, most-snipped and densest episodes, new shows, one-and-done shows, weekday rhythm, monthly chart, top tags, books and guests, year-over-year
Shows table gains average episode length and snips-per-episode alongside snips-per-hour
Tags, snips-per-episode and average lengths are all exportable; a whole tag exports as one Markdown file
